name: Bhavnath Mandir Food Stalls
signature_dish: Maggi, masala chai, and chaas before the climb
why_it_matters: Bhavnath is the start point of the Girnar climb (10,000 steps to Datta Shikhar). The food-stall cluster around Bhavnath Mahadev temple is where every climber loads up at 4am-5am before starting the trek. Mostly carts and small kitchens run by families on rotating shifts. Chai, maggi, fafda-jalebi, vada-pav — climber food, designed for energy and quick consumption. Stalls are cheapest before the climb; prices double once you cross the gate.
insider_tip: Start before 5am to beat the heat. The chai before the climb is cheaper and stronger than the mid-trail stalls. Carry a 1L water bottle from a closed/sealed cart, not the open jugs (hygiene is poor on the open carts). Cash only.
signature_address: Bhavnath Road, Girnar Taleti, Junagadh, Gujarat 362001

name: Girnar Ropeway Base Canteen
area: Girnar Ropeway Lower Station, Bhavnath Road
why_it_matters: The Girnar Ropeway opened October 2020 — the canteen at the lower station catches every ropeway visitor who skips the step climb. Standard cafeteria-style — hot snacks, tea, packaged drinks. Cleaner and faster than the trail stalls; built for queue-management, not destination dining.
insider_tip: Pre-ropeway breakfast is the right slot — climb to top via ropeway, eat at the top after seeing the temples; come back hungry to the base canteen. The thali is decent for the price (₹120-150). Avoid the cold drinks displayed in the open sun.
signature_address: Girnar Ropeway Lower Station, Bhavnath Road, Girnar Taleti, Junagadh, Gujarat 362001

name: Mid-Trail Tea Stalls (4,000-step plateau)
area: Between Mali Parab and Jain Temple Cluster
why_it_matters: On the plateau at roughly the 4,000-step mark where the Jain temple complex sits, a cluster of stalls sells fruit, water, lemon juice, buttermilk and biscuits to climbers. This is the last meaningful food zone — stalls beyond step 7,000 are inconsistent or absent. Locals carrying the goods up by hand and donkey; prices reflect that (3x base rates).
insider_tip: Stock up here, not above — there's nothing reliable past step 7,000. Buttermilk (chaas) is the best electrolyte for the heat; better than the bottled energy drinks. Carry small notes; vendors don't make change for ₹500 readily. No UPI at most stalls.
signature_address: Girnar Trail, Around Mali Parab Plateau, Approximately 4,000-step mark, Junagadh, Gujarat 362001

name: Geeta Lodge (post-climb lunch)
why_it_matters: Geeta Lodge is in Junagadh town, ~5km from Bhavnath/Girnar Taleti — it's the obvious recovery-meal after the Girnar climb. Climbers descend by 11am-1pm; Geeta is open by 11:30am with hot unlimited thali for ₹150. Founded 1938. The Kathiyawadi-style thali (spicier, less sweet than mainland Gujarati) replenishes calories spent on the climb.
insider_tip: Auto-rickshaw from Bhavnath to Mullawada is ₹100-150; share with other climbers descending at the same time. Ask for double rotla and extra buttermilk after the climb — you'll burn through both. Geeta closes at 3pm for lunch break before reopening at 7pm for dinner.
signature_address: Baliya Dharmashala Building, Railway Station Road, Mullawada, Junagadh, Gujarat 362001
